article.title: Separating Transfers, Spending, and Shared Expenses in Household Finance

paragraphs.en: Household budgets become confusing when every movement of money is treated as spending. Moving funds from a bank account to a prepaid wallet reduces the bank balance, but it does not immediately reduce the household's wealth. The money has changed location, not purpose. A purchase made later with that wallet is the actual expense. If the transfer and the purchase are both recorded as spending, the budget counts the same economic event twice. The first principle of accurate household accounting is therefore to distinguish a transfer between owned accounts from a payment to an outside party.
paragraphs.zh: 當家庭把所有金錢流動都當支出，預算就會混亂。銀行轉入預付錢包使銀行餘額減少，卻沒有立即減少家庭財富，只是資金位置改變。之後用錢包購物才是真正支出。若轉入和購物都記成消費，同一經濟事件就被算兩次。首要原則是區分自有帳戶間轉移與對外付款。
paragraphs.ja: 家計では口座間の資金移動と実際の支出を区別します。銀行からプリペイド残高への移動は資産の置き場所を変えるだけです。その後の買い物が費用です。両方を支出にすると二重計上になります。

paragraphs.en: Consider a credit card used to fund a digital account that subsequently transfers value to a prepaid payment service. The card charge creates an obligation to the issuer, while the digital account or prepaid balance represents an asset that can be used later. The intermediate movement should be labeled as funding or transfer according to the system's accounting model, not automatically as a restaurant or grocery expense. When the card bill is settled, the payment reduces cash and the outstanding liability. It should not create a second expense if the underlying purchase was already recognized. Timing differences make this distinction essential.
paragraphs.zh: 例如信用卡先為數位帳戶入金，再把價值轉到預付支付服務。信用卡刷款形成對發卡機構的負債，數位帳戶或預付餘額則是日後可用資產。中間移動應依帳務模型標記為入金或資金移轉，不能自動算餐飲或雜貨消費。繳信用卡帳單是減少現金與未清負債，若原消費已入帳，不應再形成第二筆支出。時間差讓區分格外重要。
paragraphs.ja: カードでデジタル口座に入金し、さらにプリペイド残高へ移す場合、カード債務と利用可能残高が生じます。途中の移動を食費などに分類してはいけません。カード返済も元の購入を計上済みなら新たな費用ではありません。

paragraphs.en: Shared expenses introduce another layer. Suppose one partner pays a dinner bill for both people. The full amount leaves that partner's account, but only the agreed personal share is their economic burden. The remaining portion is a receivable from the other partner if reimbursement is expected. When the reimbursement arrives, it settles the receivable rather than creating new income. The reverse situation also matters: if a partner pays on your behalf, your share is an expense and a payable to that partner, even though your own bank account has not yet changed. A clear record separates the person who paid from the person who ultimately bears the cost.
paragraphs.zh: 均分支出還有另一層。若一人先付兩人的晚餐，整筆從他的帳戶流出，但按約定只有自己的份額是個人負擔。預期對方償還的部分是應收款，收到還款是結清應收而非新收入。反過來，伴侶替你付費時，你的份額是支出與對伴侶的應付款，即使銀行尚未扣款。紀錄應分開「誰付款」與「誰最終負擔」。
paragraphs.ja: 割り勘では支払者と費用負担者を分けます。一方が全額立て替えた場合、相手の負担分は未収金です。返金は新しい収入ではなく未収金の精算です。逆に相手が立て替えた自分の分は、口座からまだ出金していなくても費用と未払金になります。

paragraphs.en: Labels should describe economic meaning rather than merely the payment instrument. A transaction called 'Card A' says how money moved but not whether it was a purchase, transfer, reimbursement, or advance. A better model records several dimensions: transaction type, source and destination accounts, payer, beneficiary, owner of the expense, and settlement status. Not every application needs all these fields on screen. However, the underlying data should preserve distinctions that affect balances and forecasts. Otherwise, convenient shortcuts today may create reconciliation problems when the household reviews a year of activity.
paragraphs.zh: 標籤應描述經濟意義，不只是支付工具。寫「A卡」只能看出怎麼付，無法知道是購買、轉帳、報銷還是代墊。較好的模型可記交易類型、來源和目的帳戶、付款人、受益人、支出歸屬及結算狀態。畫面不必全部顯示，但底層資料應保留會影響餘額和預測的差異，避免日後對帳困難。
paragraphs.ja: 支払手段だけでは取引の意味が分かりません。購入、振替、立替、精算を区別し、口座、支払者、負担者、精算状況を記録します。画面は簡潔でも、残高や予測に必要な意味はデータに残すべきです。

paragraphs.en: Forecasting adds a time dimension. A transfer between owned accounts may change where liquidity is available without changing total household assets. A credit card purchase may affect spending immediately but reduce bank cash only on a later payment date. A reimbursement expected next month can improve the forecast, yet it should remain distinct from money already received. To avoid false confidence, forecasts should show confirmed obligations separately from uncertain incoming payments. A single balance cannot answer every question. Users may need both a consolidated asset view and an account-specific cash-flow view to know whether an upcoming bill can be paid.
paragraphs.zh: 預測還涉及時間。自有帳戶轉移改變可用現金所在位置，卻不改變總資產。信用卡購買立即形成支出，銀行現金則在日後扣款。預期下月收到的代墊還款可影響預測，但須與已收到的錢分開。確定義務與不確定入金應分開顯示。單一餘額不能回答所有問題，需同時看合併資產及各帳戶現金流，才能知道帳單能否支付。
paragraphs.ja: 予測では時点が重要です。振替は資金の場所を変え、カード購入は費用発生と銀行引落日がずれます。予定の立替精算は受領済み資金と区別します。総資産と口座別資金繰りの両方を確認します。

paragraphs.en: Reconciliation is the practical test of the model. Bank statements, card statements, and prepaid transaction histories should explain the movements shown in the household ledger. Every external expense should appear once in the chosen accounting view, while internal transfers should connect matching accounts. Differences may arise from pending charges, fees, refunds, currency conversion, or timing. Investigating them requires stable identifiers and a clear audit trail. The objective is not to make every screen show the same number. It is to ensure that each number answers a defined question and can be traced to evidence.
paragraphs.zh: 對帳是模型的實務考驗。銀行、信用卡及預付交易明細應能解釋家庭台帳的資金流。每筆對外支出在所選帳務視角應只出現一次，內部轉移要連結對應帳戶。待入帳、手續費、退款、匯率及時間差都可能造成差異。調查需要穩定識別碼和稽核軌跡。目標不是所有畫面數字相同，而是每個數字回答明確問題且可追溯。
paragraphs.ja: 照合では銀行、カード、プリペイドの明細と家計台帳を突き合わせます。外部支出は一度だけ計上し、内部振替は対応する口座を結びます。手数料、返金、為替、時点差を調べられる履歴が必要です。
